A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GazeReward with the same authors, framework and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including identification of removed and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model experiments on OASST1, HelpSteer2 and RewardBench in Tables 3–5, together with component comparisons and appendix hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original OASST1 and HelpSteer2 results summarized over three seeds in Tables 3–4 and retains the RewardBench results and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: GazeConcat, GazeAdd, the projector architecture and reward loss remain unchanged. However, v1 explicitly trains the ET projector in Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1.4; v2 removes both statements and says the ET modules remain frozen. Appendix A.1.5 specifies only that the predictor is frozen, leaving unclear whether projector training actually changed or its description became imprecise.

E1.justification: Both versions use English OASST1 and HelpSteer2 for reward modeling and RewardBench for additional evaluation. The gaze predictors use the same Dundee, GECO, ZuCo and Provo corpora. Newly reported predictor errors do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same no-gaze reward-model baselines using Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B. The integration and feature variants are also retained, including unavailable Mistral GazeAdd results. The new predictor-error table introduces no reward-model comparator.

E3.justification: The stated dataset splits, preference-accuracy metric, backbone checkpoints, two-epoch budget, QLoRA settings, hyperparameter search and checkpoint-selection procedure are unchanged. Three-seed reporting belongs to E5; the newly stated predictor test split documents an existing pretrained component rather than establishing a revised evaluation.

E4.justification: The same initialization, integration-method and feature-combination comparisons are retained. The cucumber-response gaze example and learning-rate, batch-size and scheduler analyses in Figures 3–7 are unchanged. Revised scores do not introduce a new ablation or robustness question.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without run-count or uncertainty information for the main results. v2 Section 4.2 first reports three seeds, and Tables 3–4 add ± quantities and significance stars throughout. This substantially changes statistical reporting, although the uncertainty measure, statistical test and star thresholds are unspecified. The PDFs do not establish an increase from a particular earlier run count.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 replace earlier values with three-seed summaries and materially change gains and rankings. For OASST1/Llama-3-8B, the baseline changes from 58.6 to 65.5±2.1 and GazeConcat fcomb2.2 from 73.1 to 71.2±0.8, reducing the reported relative gain from 24.8% to 8.8%. GazeAdd fcomb2.5 with Llama-3-8B-Instruct changes from 51.9 to 70.2±0.1, reversing its below-baseline finding. These are revised reported estimates, not established same-setting performance improvements. RewardBench Table 5 is unchanged; Appendix A.1.2 adds predictor MSE/MAE results.

T1.justification: The Bradley–Terry formulation, reward loss, embedding operations and token-mapping mathematics are retained. Changing the description of w from time steps to tokens clarifies existing notation without changing the mathematical definition. No theorem or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the headline accuracy-gain contribution from over 20% to over 10%. The central claims of a scalable gaze-augmented reward framework and improved preference prediction remain, as does the abstract's overall contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 weakens the interpretation that unaligned models benefit more to saying they can benefit. The new Section 5.1 acknowledges the method's additional parameters relative to the baseline, and the Impact Statement adds bias inherited from human feedback and ET-model training data. Existing language, data-contamination and downstream-alignment limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 supplies a repository URL and states that reproduction code is available. Appendices A.1.2 and C add predictor sizes of 17.5M and 125M parameters, a 0.53M-parameter projector and predictor evaluation details. Conversely, explicit disclosure that the projector is trained without adapters disappears. Backbone checkpoint links are mainly relocated, while hardware and training-time information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The dedicated Related Work section is removed without an appendix replacement, eliminating the reward-modeling and gaze-NLP survey and the detailed distinction from Kiegeland et al.'s dataset-generation approach. Associated references, including Lightman, Uesato and LLM-Blender, disappear. This substantially reduces research positioning beyond the separate bibliographic metadata updates.

P1.justification: The ending is substantially reorganized: the Related Work section disappears, while v2 contains near-duplicate Discussion and Limitations sections numbered 5/5.1 and 6/6.1. It also introduces an appendix Models subsection, condenses long reference author lists, adds acknowledgments and an acceptance notice, and makes smaller wording corrections.

P2.justification: Tables 3–4 are expanded to display uncertainty and significance markers, and a small predictor-MAE table is added as Table 6. Existing appendix tables are renumbered, and several tables, plots and the code listing move. Figures 1–7 retain their substantive visual content; the overall single-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: Three-seed summaries, a stated code-access location and parameter counts improve transparency. However, uncertainty and significance notation remain undefined, and the retained claim that fcomb2.5 underperforms baselines conflicts with the updated reported means. Removing detailed related-work positioning, duplicating Discussion/Limitations and obscuring projector training also weaken clarity. These material benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
